metadata.title: Digital Medication Management Residuality Stress Test
metadata.description: Explore how medication-management services would need to change when patients become isolated, prescriptions change after packing, cognitive ability declines, funding depends on outcomes, medicines are recalled, or consumer competitors reshape the channel.
metadata.naiveArchitecture: A care professional configures a patient's medication schedule in a portal. A connected home device dispenses the prepared pouch at the scheduled time, records confirmation, and sends a missed-dose alarm to a carer.
metadata.residualArchitecture: Instead of treating the portal schedule, medicine pouches, device actions, patient confirmation, and care escalation as one current plan, the adapted design keeps each as a separate, versioned record. The device can continue safely offline from a signed plan; prescription changes identify the exact affected doses; dispensing is not confused with proof of ingestion; and every transition can be reconciled across pharmacy, care, patient, and funding records.
metadata.note: The stressors are centered on the care and medication context, not a list of infrastructure failures. Candidate residues are design hypotheses and do not claim clinical implementation or regulatory approval.

source.title: Residues: Time, Change, and Uncertainty in Software Architecture
source.author: Barry M. O'Reilly

stressors.name: A winter storm isolates patients at home without power or connectivity for three days
stressors.detection: Weather and civil-protection alerts, device power state, missed heartbeats, battery telemetry, local interaction events, and care-provider welfare checks.
stressors.attractor: The home device becomes the only immediately available medication support while carers, pharmacy deliveries, cloud decisions, and video assistance may all be unreachable.
stressors.businessReaction: Preserve safe scheduled dispensing locally, communicate remaining autonomy, prevent ambiguous plan changes, give the patient an offline help path, and reconcile all evidence when contact returns.
stressors.residue: Deploy a signed, bounded medication plan with effective times, local schedule, policy, stock state, battery horizon, and emergency instructions. The device records an append-only local dose ledger and reconciles idempotently; cloud reachability is not the authority to dispense a currently valid dose.

impacts.effect: Independent living includes a defined safe-autonomy horizon when home and care connectivity disappear.
Reliable dosing continues from the last signed plan rather than stopping because the cloud is unavailable.
Offers local instructions and a pre-agreed escalation path that does not assume an online carer.
Continued service on device must distinguish safe local autonomy from merely appearing connected.
Shows the patient remaining power, plan validity, stock horizon, and offline help instructions.
Verifies and executes a bounded signed plan locally and preserves an append-only event history.
Publishes effective, versioned plans with explicit offline validity and transition rules.
Reports autonomy horizon and performs conflict-safe replay instead of treating heartbeat loss as the whole state.
Owns safe local execution, power behavior, and auditable reconnection.
Keeps a scheduled dose safe and explainable through bounded offline operation and later reconciliation.
Makes multi-day offline medication continuity a home-dispensing benchmark.

stressors.name: A clinician changes the prescription after the current pouch roll has been packed
stressors.detection: e-Prescription update, clinician order, pharmacy notification, patient discharge, medication reconciliation, and mismatch between packed and active regimen.
stressors.attractor: The clinically valid regimen, physically available pouches, device schedule, and carer expectation disagree; blindly continuing or replacing data in place can both create a medication error.
stressors.businessReaction: Establish the effective clinical transition, identify affected pouches and doses, pause or substitute safely, coordinate repacking or manual support, and prove which instruction governed each dispense decision.
stressors.residue: Model prescriptions and regimens as immutable versions with effective intervals and supersession reasons. Every pouch, planned dose, device plan, dispense event, and exception references its governing version; reconciliation drives quarantine, replacement, controlled overlap, and human escalation.

impacts.effect: Prescription-accurate packing includes controlled transitions after a roll has left the pharmacy.
Order alignment becomes a continuous clinical-version reconciliation job, not a batch handoff.
Shows affected doses, transition authority, stock disposition, replacement, and care escalation as one case.
Packing efficiency must be balanced with safe mid-cycle change and avoidable repack work.
Coordinates immutable prescription versions, pouch lineage, transition cases, and pharmacy fulfillment.
Imports clinical changes as new effective versions and preserves source authority and reason.
Relates each packed order and pouch run to the regimen version it was intended to fulfill.
Finds the exact ordered, packed, loaded, planned, and dispensed set affected by a transition.
Owns the cross-boundary transition workflow and pouch disposition evidence with scheduling.
Makes pharmacy-to-device reconciliation depth a differentiator against institutional medication automation.
Carries the prescription change from clinical source through packing, device plan, exceptions, and replacement.

stressors.name: A patient's cognitive decline makes button confirmation unreliable evidence of ingestion
stressors.detection: Care observations, repeated interaction anomalies, dose-taken disputes, clinical review, alarm patterns, and consented assisted-session evidence.
stressors.attractor: The product reports adherence while the patient's ability to understand, retrieve, and ingest the dose has changed; the normal self-service interaction becomes false reassurance to carers.
stressors.businessReaction: Reassess the support level, distinguish dispense from ingestion confidence, adapt reminders and assistance, involve authorized carers, and escalate the care plan when evidence is insufficient.
stressors.residue: Represent adherence as a chain of evidence with type, source, confidence, consent, and observation time. A governed support profile selects reminder, confirmation, video, carer, and visit paths; no single device action is permanently equated with ingestion.

impacts.effect: Remote caseload confidence is based on evidence quality and changing patient capability, not a binary device event.
Nurses can identify patients whose evidence no longer supports remote-only care.
Prioritizes visits using evidence confidence, patient support profile, and recent change rather than missed doses alone.
Staff use should be evaluated against appropriate intervention and evidence interpretation, not portal login alone.
Shows evidence type, confidence, change trend, consent, and the active support profile for each patient.
Stores dispense, retrieval, confirmation, observation, and clinical assessment as distinct evidence.
Provides an assisted evidence channel under explicit consent and retention policy.
Routes low-confidence or changing evidence according to patient support policy, not only missed timing.
Owns evidence semantics and escalation thresholds with clinical safety governance.
Raises assisted interaction and evidence quality as a benchmark beyond automated dispensing.
Turns changing adherence evidence into a governed caseload decision and appropriate intervention.

stressors.name: A municipality pays only for verified medication outcomes and avoided care visits
stressors.detection: Tender documents, payer workshops, reimbursement rules, procurement scoring, outcome-audit requests, and contract-renewal negotiations.
stressors.attractor: Revenue and program survival depend on defensible outcomes across cohorts, while device activity alone cannot prove adherence improvement, avoided visits, causality, or fair comparison.
stressors.businessReaction: Define measurable outcomes with the buyer, capture consented evidence, preserve cohort and intervention context, report limitations, and reconcile service payment to the agreed outcome contract.
stressors.residue: Introduce a versioned outcome contract linking population, eligibility, baseline, intervention, evidence, metric definition, attribution rule, reporting window, privacy basis, and payment term. Operational events remain raw facts; derived outcomes are reproducible governed views.

impacts.effect: Provable safety and cost-to-serve become contract execution, not retrospective presentation work.
Funders and regulators receive reproducible measures tied to the exact cohort and service contract.
Every reported result links to metric definition, input evidence, exclusions, consent, and audit trail.
Organization retention can be related to agreed outcome fulfillment rather than device count alone.
Needs outcome-contract authoring, cohort versioning, reproducible analysis, evidence quality, and audit exports.
Separates immutable operational facts from governed outcome definitions and derived evidence.
Carries privacy basis, consent, access, purpose, and derivation evidence into outcome reporting.
Owns reproducibility and evidence quality while care and commercial owners define outcome meaning.
Supplies the governed intervention and caseload evidence from which contracted outcomes are derived.
Makes reproducible care-outcome evidence a benchmark for remote medication services.

stressors.name: A medicine lot in loaded pouch rolls is recalled overnight
stressors.detection: Pharmacy and manufacturer notice, regulator alert, lot evidence, prescription matching, pouch lineage, and device inventory reconciliation.
stressors.attractor: Affected doses are distributed across homes, some devices are offline, and the next scheduled dispense may occur before a carer or replacement roll can arrive.
stressors.businessReaction: Identify affected patients and doses, stop unsafe dispensing even while disconnected, preserve unaffected medication where clinically allowed, arrange replacement or assisted dosing, and prove complete remediation.
stressors.residue: No new structural change is required: versioned regimen and pouch lineage identify the affected set, while the signed local-plan transition can quarantine future doses on each device and retain an auditable offline decision until reconciliation.

impacts.effect: The existing lineage and transition model can scope and replace affected pouches precisely.
Produces the patient, device, pouch, dose, dispense, and replacement set from the same reconciliation graph.
Supply continuity can distinguish safe replacement coverage from continued use of recalled stock.
Coordinates recall scope and replacement through the existing regimen-transition case.
Resolves all loaded and dispensed doses linked to the recalled lot.
Applies the signed quarantine transition locally and records the decision while offline.
Can execute the recall through existing lineage, transition, and local-control contracts.
Makes end-to-end recall traceability from pharmacy lot to home dispense a defensible safety benchmark.
Pharmacy safety extends from packed production lots to every loaded and potentially dispensed home dose.
Reuses pouch lineage and device reconciliation to quarantine, replace, and verify every affected dose.

stressors.name: A pharmacy chain bundles a consumer dispenser at no upfront cost
stressors.detection: Pharmacy tenders, consumer offers, care-provider churn interviews, pricing comparisons, prescription-transfer patterns, and new device activations.
stressors.attractor: Hardware price disappears as a barrier and the pharmacy owns enrollment, refill, and recurring customer contact; a device-centric proposition loses against a bundled medication service.
stressors.businessReaction: Compete on clinical continuity, care workflow, open pharmacy integration, measurable outcomes, and service portability; support channel partnerships without surrendering patient consent or evidence continuity.
stressors.residue: Separate device, service entitlement, care organization, pharmacy supplier, payer, patient, and evidence custodian. A patient service record can change device or supply partner while consented medication history, regimen transitions, alarms, and outcome evidence remain continuous.

impacts.effect: The value proposition shifts from procuring devices to governing a portable, evidence-backed medication service.
Rollout can combine devices and pharmacies without fragmenting safety, access, and outcome governance.
Provisioning binds a patient service entitlement to replaceable device and pharmacy providers.
Devices deployed becomes a channel measure beneath active, safe patient service rather than the sole growth outcome.
Must participate in a portable multi-device service model instead of depending on vertically owned hardware.
Binds patient, consent, service entitlement, device, pharmacy, payer, and care organization independently.
Makes provider and device transitions explicit while preserving clinical and operational continuity.
Owns portable service identity and partner boundaries across a changing channel model.
Frames consumer-device competition around channel ownership and service continuity rather than hardware features alone.
Separates enrollment and service continuity from the current pharmacy and device bundle.
